papers.title_in_file: Preparing for Post-Quantum Critical Infrastructure: Assessments of Quantum Computing Vulnerabilities of National Critical Functions: Appendix
papers.what_it_is: Appendix B of a 2022 RAND Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center report that rates, for each of the 55 U.S. national critical functions, the urgency, scope, cost, other factors and priority for assistance of quantum computing vulnerabilities.

assertions.value: The appendix contains assessments of the quantum computing vulnerabilities affecting each of the 55 national critical functions (NCFs), intended to help CISA understand the issues and prioritize U.S. government assistance to infrastructure owners and operators.
quotes: This appendix contains assessments of the quantum computing vulnerabilities affecting each of the 55 NCFs.
These assessments are intended to help CISA understand the issues affecting each NCF and prioritize U.S. government assistance to critical infrastructure owners and operators.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is a project of the Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center for the National Risk Management Center of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and that the results do not necessarily reflect official DHS opinion or policy.
quotes: The Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center (HSOAC) is carrying out a project entitled “National Critical Function Emerging Risk Analysis” for the National Risk Management Center (NRMC) of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
The results presented in this report do not necessarily reflect official DHS opinion or policy.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own sponsor and disclaimer here.

assertions.value: The document states that the research was published in 2022 and was approved for public release.
quotes: This research was published in 2022. Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope here.

assertions.value: The authors use a scope scale in which at least 100 organizations that must take meaningful action is the threshold for a rating of high scope, and between ten and 100 organizations is medium scope.
assertions.anchor: NCF 53 Scope, p.NCF53-2; NCF 7 Scope, p.NCF07-2
quotes: is likely well above the threshold (at least 100 organizations) for a rating of high scope.
we estimated that between ten and 100 separate organizations in this NCF operate satellites for communication purposes
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the scope thresholds in the assessments themselves.

assertions.value: The authors define a moderate confidentiality lifetime as one to ten years and a long confidentiality lifetime as more than ten years.
assertions.anchor: NCF 43 Synopsis, p.NCF43-1; NCF 13 Urgency, p.NCF13-2
quotes: very few trade secrets are expected to have a long confidentiality lifetime (i.e., more than ten years), although trade secrets with a moderate confidentiality lifetime (i.e., one to ten years) will be much more common.
these data are considered to have a moderate confidentiality lifetime (i.e., one to ten years)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the lifetimes in the assessment text.

assertions.value: The authors state that, like in many other assessments, they assumed that IT products and services enabling the PQC migration become available quickly after the NIST PQC standardization project ends, so that organizations can wait until planned end of life of hardware to replace it.
quotes: Like with many other assessments, we assumed that information technology products and services that enable the migration to PQC would be available quickly after the completion of the National Institute of Standards and Technology PQC standardization project and that organizations can therefore wait
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the assumption behind its cost and scope ratings.

assertions.value: The authors state that authentication vulnerabilities in defense-related systems are just-in-time risks that can be addressed any time before a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists, while holding that every remote authentication mode must migrate to PQC before then.
quotes: Although these are just-in-time risks that can be addressed any time before the advent of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, it is critical to the functioning of the NCF that every mode of remote authentication for defense-related systems be migrated to PQC before then.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own framing of authentication risk here.

assertions.value: The authors rate the Operate Core Network function low on urgency, scope, cost and priority for assistance, and say networks should plan to implement PQC where public-key cryptography authenticates routing information using the border gateway protocol.
assertions.anchor: NCF 1 Summary and Priority, pp.NCF01-1 and NCF01-2
quotes: Networks should make plans to implement post-quantum cryptography (PQC) where public-key cryptography is used to authenticate routing information using the border gateway protocol.
We rated the NCF as a low priority for assistance because of the consistently low ratings in each category and the presence of other strong risk-mitigating factors.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors report that approximately ten organizations provide core network operations for the Internet backbone nationally, which underlies their low scope rating for the function.
quotes: Our assessment is that scope for this NCF is low. Nationally, approximately ten organizations provide core network operations for the Internet backbone (Greene, 2020).
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the core network function does not use or control data with a long confidentiality lifetime in its own operations and so presents no clear catch-and-exploit vulnerability.
quotes: In its own operations, the NCF does not use or control data with a long confidentiality lifetime
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that an attacker with a quantum computer could exploit vulnerable certificates at several points in the DOCSIS certificate chain (root certificate authority, trusted manufacturer, operator or device) unless they are replaced with quantum-resistant versions.
quotes: An attacker with a quantum computer could exploit the vulnerability in these certificates at multiple points in this chain (root certificate authority, trusted manufacturer, operator, or device), unless each of these certificates is replaced with a quantum-resistant version.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the symmetric-key encryption cable operators use between modems and the terminal network system is not a significant quantum computing vulnerability.
quotes: That encryption is not a significant vulnerability with respect to quantum computing, however, because it uses symmetric-key cryptography.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors rate the Provide Cable Access Network Services function low on urgency, high on scope and cost, and medium on priority for assistance, because of the expected scope and cost of updates despite mitigating factors.
assertions.anchor: NCF 2 Urgency, Scope, Priority, pp.NCF02-2 and NCF02-3
quotes: Our assessment is that urgency of action for this NCF is low. No catch-and-exploit issues are apparent
We rated the NCF as a medium priority for assistance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that certificate authorities might need to deploy and sign hundreds of millions of new certificates, and that operators and manufacturers might need several strategies to deploy upgrades remotely while keeping backward compatibility.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that vulnerable cryptographic systems are typically embedded in hardware at production and that hardware can be in use for 20 or more years, though mechanisms exist for gradually addressing the vulnerabilities after deployment.
quotes: that hardware can be in use for long durations (i.e., 20 or more years), mechanisms exist for gradually addressing those vulnerabilities after deployment
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that Internet based content, information and communication services is one of the national critical functions most affected by vulnerabilities from quantum computers, and rate it high on urgency and scope, medium on cost, and high on priority for assistance.
assertions.anchor: NCF 3 Synopsis and Summary, pp.NCF03-1 to NCF03-4
quotes: This NCF is one of those most affected by the vulnerabilities from quantum computers.
Our assessment is that urgency of action for this NCF is high.
We rated the NCF as a high priority for assistance.

assertions.value: The authors state that nearly every current presumed secure Internet interaction will present an authentication vulnerability once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that migrations to new standards have historically taken decades and that supporting this function in beginning the PQC transition quickly is imperative.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that hybrid schemes combining conventional cryptography and PQC algorithms will likely be needed, that their formats and requirements are still being developed and tested, and that the NIST post-quantum algorithms are generally more computationally demanding.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that many other NCFs depend heavily on this function, so delays in its PQC migration would leave enduring vulnerability in the NCFs that use its products and services.
quotes: Many other NCFs are highly dependent on this NCF.

Delays in migration to PQC and the provision of products and services that facilitate quantum-safe communication and collaboration will create enduring vulnerability in other NCFs that use those products and services.

quotes: Networks should make plans to implement post-quantum cryptography (PQC) where public-key cryptography is used to authenticate routing information using the border gateway protocol.
We rated the NCF as a low priority for assistance because of the consistently low ratings in each category and the presence of other strong risk-mitigating factors.

assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own assessment, not tested by an experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that they identified no catch-and-exploit vulnerabilities for positioning, navigation and timing, and expect authentication vulnerabilities to be addressed before a capable quantum computer exists.
